Description: WE PROPOSE TO INVESTIGATE GRAIN MIGRATION IN THE PROTOPLANETARY DISK DURING THE ERA OF CHONDRULE FORMATION BY INVESTIGATING THE CHEMICAL AND O-ISOTOPE COMPOSITIONS OF CHONDRULE PRECURSORS. WHILE THE DISCOVERY OF CALCIUM-ALUMINUM RICH INCLUSIONS AND CHONDRULE-LIKE OBJECTS IN COMET WILD 2 SHOWED THAT OUTWARD MIGRATION OF SUB-MM SIZED-PARTICLES OCCURRED VERY EARLY IN THE SOLAR SYSTEM  THE EXTENT AND DIRECTION(S) OF MIGRATION AFTER THIS EARLY TIME IN SOLAR SYSTEM HISTORY IS NOT KNOWN. THE PROPOSED WORK IS RELEVANT TO THE SCOPE OF THE EMERGING WORLDS PROGRAM  AS ITS GOAL IS   TO ADVANCE SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE OF THE SOLAR SYSTEM BY INVESTIGATING HOW IT FORMED AND EVOLVED  THROUGH THE ANALYSES OF EXTRATERRESTRIAL MATERIALS IN THE LABORATORY. EMERGING WORLDS IS MOST APPROPRIATE FOR THIS RESEARCH SINCE IT IS RELEVANT TO MULTIPLE TOPICS LISTED IN THE PROGRAM S SCOPE IN C.2.  INCLUDING  BUT NOT LIMITED TO:  STUDIES OF ALL ASPECTS OF MATERIALS PRESENT AND PROCESSES OCCURRING IN AND AFFECTING THE PROTOPLANETARY DISK  . WE WILL ACHIEVE THESE GOALS BY DETERMINING THE MORPHOLOGIES  ELEMENTAL  AND O-ISOTOPE COMPOSITIONS OF CHONDRULE PRECURSORS USING STATE-OF-THE-ART COORDINATED MICROANALYTICAL TECHNIQUES (FIELD EMISSION ELECTRON PROBE MICROANALYSIS AND SECONDARY ION MASS SPECTROMETRY). PARTIALLY MELTED CHONDRULES CONTAIN UNMELTED CHONDRULE PRECURSOR SILICATES THAT SURVIVED HEATING DURING CHONDRULE FORMATION  WHICH ARE TERMED RELICT GRAINS. THESE RELICT GRAINS MAY BE PRIMORDIAL SILICATES RELATED TO REFRACTORY INCLUSIONS  RECYCLED CHONDRULE FRAGMENTS FROM THE SAME METEORITE GROUP  XENOCRYSTS FROM ANOTHER CHONDRITE GROUP  OR DEBRIS FROM DIFFERENTIATED/ UNDIFFERENTIATED PLANETESIMALS. CHONDRULES FROM DISTINCT METEORITE GROUPS HAVE CHARACTERISTIC CHEMICAL AND/OR O-ISOTOPE COMPOSITIONS  ALLOWING US TO IDENTIFY THE ORIGIN(S) OF RELICT GRAINS. RELICT GRAINS IN CHONDRULES ARE IMPORTANT TO STUDY BECAUSE WE KNOW THEY WERE PRESENT DURING CHONDRULE FORMATION IN THE EARLY SOLAR SYSTEM. BY CONSTRAINING THE ORIGIN(S) OF RELICT GRAINS IN CHONDRULES FROM METEORITE GROUPS WITH DISTINCT ESTABLISHED FORMATION AGES THAT FORMED AT DISTINCT RADIAL LOCATIONS IN THE PROTOPLANETARY DISK  WE WILL INVESTIGATE GRAIN MIGRATION BETWEEN CHONDRITE GROUPS PRIOR TO AND DURING CHONDRULE FORMATION AND CONSTRAIN THEIR SOURCE(S). OUR PRELIMINARY DATA INDICATE THAT CHONDRULE FRAGMENTS MIGRATED BETWEEN DISTINCT CHONDRULE-FORMING REGIONS  FROM THE NON-CARBONACEOUS [NC] METEORITE REGION IN THE INNER SOLAR SYSTEM TO THE CARBONACEOUS CHONDRITE [CC] METEORITE REGION IN THE OUTER SOLAR SYSTEM REGION  IMPLYING OUTWARD MIGRATION OF GRAINS IN THE PROTOPLANETARY DISK. OUR DATA WILL HAVE SIGNIFICANT IMPLICATIONS FOR MIXING OF MATERIAL IN THE EARLY SOLAR SYSTEM  AND ASSUMING 26AL HOMOGENEITY  PROVIDE ESTIMATES ON THE TIMING OF SUCH MIGRATION(S) BETWEEN FORMATION REGIONS. DETERMINING THE ORIGIN(S) OF CHONDRULE PRECURSORS  RELICT GRAINS  WILL PROVIDE ANALYTICAL CONSTRAINTS TO TEST OUR HYPOTHESIS THAT THE RADIAL MIGRATION OF GRAINS IN THE PROTOPLANETARY DISK DURING THE ERA OF CHONDRULE FORMATION WAS OUTWARD.

US DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES ET AL., 1:25-CV-11048 (D. MASS).THERE IS A COMPELLING NEED FOR INTENSIVE STUDY OF CONVECTIVE IMPACTS ON THE SUMMER STRATOSPHERE OVER NORTH AMERICA. EACH SUMMER THE NORTH AMERICAN MONSOON ANTICYCLONE (NAMA) DOMINATES THE CIRCULATION OF THE NORTH-WESTERN HEMISPHERE AND ACTS TO PARTIALLY CONFINE AND ISOLATE AIR FROM THE SURROUNDING ATMOSPHERE. STRONG CONVECTIVE STORMS IN THE NAMA REGULARLY PENETRATE DEEP INTO THE LOWER STRATOSPHERE (LS), WITH SOME ASCENDING ABOVE 20 KM (~450 K POTENTIAL TEMPERATURE). THE UNIQUENESS OF THE NAMA REGION IS MOST EASILY SEEN IN SATELLITE MEASUREMENTS OF WATER VAPOR, WHICH SHOW A LARGE ENHANCEMENT IN THE LS OVER NORTH AMERICA NOT SEEN EITHER IN MAGNITUDE OR AT SUCH HIGH LATITUDES ELSEWHERE AROUND THE GLOBE. BUT THE COUPLING OF TROPOPAUSE-PENETRATING CONVECTION WITH LARGE-SCALE MONSOONAL MOTION IS POORLY UNDERSTOOD, AS IS THE IMPACT OF CONVECTION ON THE CHEMICAL COMPOSITION OF THE LS, BOTH IN MONSOON REGIONS AND IN THE GLOBAL STRATOSPHERE, WHICH RECEIVES INPUTS OF MOIST AND POLLUTED MONSOON AIR FROM THE NAMA. THE DYNAMICS AND CHEMISTRY OF THE SUMMER STRATOSPHERE (DCOTSS) PROPOSAL DIRECTLY ADDRESSES THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP.

ACHIEVING THIS OVERARCHING OBJECTIVE WILL INVOLVE THREE MAIN TASKS: 1. DETECTING THE EXTENT OF OLIVE CROPPING SYSTEMS AND EVALUATING THE DEGREE OF CONVERSION FROM CEREAL CROPS TO OLIVES. 2. EVALUATING SOCIOECONOMIC CONDITIONS AND RISK MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES IN TWO STUDY AREAS OF MOROCCO. THIS STEP WILL FIRST INVOLVE EXPERT ELICITATION TO GROUND THE ANALYSIS IN THE REALITIES AND PERCEIVED RISKS IN THE SUPPLY CHAIN  AND WILL BE FOLLOWED BY A SERIES OF STRATIFIED SURVEYS AMONG AGRICULTURAL PRODUCERS IN TWO OLIVE PRODUCING REGIONS OF MOROCCO WHOSE AGRO-CLIMATIC CONDITIONS VARY. 3. INTEGRATING DATA ON SOCIOECONOMIC CONDITIONS WITH REMOTELY SENSED ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGES TO EVALUATE THE CORRESPONDENCE OF A REMOTELY-SENSED TRIGGER OF FARMER LOSSES DUE TO ADVERSE CONDITIONS SUCH AS DROUGHT. PERENNIAL CROPS ARE EMBLEMATIC OF THE POSSIBILITY TO ADOPT HIGHER VALUE CROPPING SYSTEMS THAT ARE OTHERWISE TOO RISKY FOR MANY FARMERS TO TAKE ON WITHOUT INSURANCE. EVEN IF THEY ARE DROUGHT-RESISTANT  PERENNIALS ARE MUCH MORE COSTLY THAN MANY ANNUAL CROPS AND INVOLVE A LONG PERIOD BEFORE THEY HAVE ECONOMICALLY-HARVESTABLE FRUITS. EVEN ONCE PRODUCING  WEATHER FLUCTUATION REMAINS A RISK: RECENT REPORTS SUGGEST MOROCCAN OLIVE FARMERS PERCEIVED YIELD DECLINES ON THE ORDER OF 36-64% LESS THAN EXPECTED IN RECENT DRY YEARS. DROUGHT CAN THEREFORE AMPLIFY RISK EXPOSURE FOR FARMERS WHEN THE FARMERS FACE HIGHER ABSOLUTE LOSSES RELATIVE TO THEIR POTENTIAL. DESPITE THE IMPORTANCE OF PERENNIALS  MOST STUDIES EVALUATING INDEXED PRODUCTS FOR AGRICULTURE FOCUS ON ANNUAL CROPPING SYSTEMS OR BROAD INDICATORS OF DROUGHT STRESS RATHER THAN THE PARTICULARS OF HIGH VALUE  LONG-TERM INVESTMENTS. THREE SENIOR COLLABORATORS FROM UC DAVIS  UMN  AND THE NATIONAL SCHOOL OF AGRICULTURE IN MEKNES  MOROCCO  WITH SIGNIFICANT ON-THE GROUND EXPERIENCE AND TECHNICAL EXPERTISE IN AGRICULTURAL ECONOMICS AND AGRONOMY WILL ADVISE THE PROJECT TO ENSURE ALIGNMENT WITH THE REALITIES OF MOROCCO S ENVIRONMENT AND POLICY CONTEXT. OUR INTERDISCIPLINARY APPROACH TO INTEGRATING SOCIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROCESSES AS WELL AS DISAGGREGATING IMPACTS ACROSS SPACE ALIGNS WITH THE LCLUC RESEARCH PRIORITIES TO UNDERSTAND THE SUSTAINABILITY  VULNERABILITY  AND RESILIENCE OF HUMAN LAND USE. FURTHERMORE  OUR RESULTS WILL BE MADE PUBLIC TO HELP ADVANCE LAND CHANGE SCIENCE AS WELL AS INFORM LAND USE POLICY IN MOROCCO  THE MEDITERRANEAN REGIONAL INFORMATION NETWORK (MEDRIN)  MORE BROADLY -- AREAS THAT HAVE BEEN EVALUATED AS HIGHLY VULNERABLE TO FUTURE CLIMATE CHANGE.

Description: THIS PROJECT PROPOSES TO UTILIZE NOVEL TAILORED IONIC LIQUID (IL) MIXTURES AS COOLANTS FOR SPACECRAFT THERMAL MANAGEMENT. ILS ARE SALTLIKE MATERIALS WITH PURELY IONIC BONDS THAT HAVE MELTING POINTS BELOW ROOM TEMPERATURE  AND SOME CAN EVEN REMAIN IN LIQUID FORM WELL BELOW 0 C. THEIR LOW MELTING POINTS ARE DUE TO THEIR HIGHLY SYMMETRIC MOLECULAR STRUCTURES  LARGE ION SIZES  CATION-ANION SIZE MISMATCH  AND STRONG IONIC INTERACTIONS. ILS EXHIBIT EUTECTIC BEHAVIOR  ALLOWING MIXTURES OF ILS TO HAVE LOWER MELTING POINTS THAN THEIR INDIVIDUAL PURE COMPOUNDS. THE PROPOSAL AIMS TO LEVERAGE THE UNIQUE CHARACTERISTIC OF ILS AND DEVELOP A CUSTOMIZED BINARY OR TERTIARY EUTECTIC IL MIXTURE WITH A MELTING POINT LOWER THAN 150 K. CURRENT COOLANTS USED IN SPACE MISSIONS HAVE LIMITATIONS  AND FINDING A SINGLE-FLUID  SINGLE-PHASE HEAT TRANSFER COOLANT THAT COULD PERFORM EFFECTIVELY ACROSS ALL TEMPERATURE RANGES WOULD BE A GAME-CHANGER FOR FUTURE SPACE MISSIONS. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL DEVELOP A SYSTEMATIC PHYSICS-BASED APPROACH TO DESIGN TAILORED IL MIXTURES WITH EXTREMELY LOW MELTING POINTS DESIGNED SPECIFICALLY FOR SINGLE-PHASE THERMAL MANAGEMENT OF SPACECRAFT IN HARSH ENVIRONMENTS. THE PROJECT WILL A) IMPLEMENT A SYSTEMATIC PHYSICS-BASED QUANTITATIVE STRUCTURE-PROPERTY RELATIONSHIP (QSPR) MODELING FRAMEWORK TO IDENTIFY BINARY AND TERTIARY EUTECTIC IL MIXTURES  B) EMPLOY STATE-OF-THE-ART MEASUREMENT TECHNIQUES TO CHARACTERIZE THE RELEVANT THERMOPHYSICAL PROPERTIES  AND C) PERFORM PROOF-OF-CONCEPT PERFORMANCE VALIDATION OF THE SELECTED IL MIXTURES VIA LABSCALE EXPERIMENTS. THE PROJECT WILL BEGIN AT TRL 1  EMPLOYING PHYSICS-DRIVEN METHODS TO IDENTIFY  SELECT  SYNTHESIZE  AND CHARACTERIZE PROMISING IL MIXTURES  AND END AT TRL 4 WITH COMPONENT LEVEL AS WELL AS SYSTEM-LEVEL PROOF-OF-CONCEPT HEAT TRANSFER PERFORMANCE VALIDATION IN THE LABORATORY ENVIRONMENT. UPON COMPLETION OF OUR PROPOSED RESEARCH  WE AIM TO PROGRESS OUR PROJECT S TRL FROM 4 TO 5-6 BY PERFORMING A TECHNOLOGY DEMONSTRATION WITH OUR INDUSTRY PARTNER  ADVANCED COOLING TECHNOLOGIES  INC.  AND 3M. THE DISCOVERY OF A SUITABLE NOVEL IL FOR SPACECRAFT THERMAL MANAGEMENT COULD HAVE A SIGNIFICANT IMPACT ON THE EFFICIENCY  FLEXIBILITY  AND SAFETY OF FUTURE SPACE MISSIONS.

Description: SCIENCE GOALS AND OBJECTIVES: ONE OF THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDINGS MADE BY PARKER SOLAR PROBE (PSP) IS THE LARGE NUMBER OF MAGNETIC SWITCHBACKS (SWITCHBACKS FOR SHORT) IN THE NEAR-SUN SPACE. SWITCHBACKS  WITH TYPICAL TIME SCALES OF MINUTES TO TENS OF MINUTES  ARE LOCAL POLARITY-REVERSALS OF THE (RADIAL) MAGNETIC FIELD AND ARE TYPICALLY HIGHLY ALFV NIC  WITH CORRELATIONS BETWEEN VELOCITY AND MAGNETIC FIELD CORRESPONDING TO LARGE-AMPLITUDE OUTWARD-PROPAGATING ALFV N WAVES. MANY OBSERVATIONAL STUDIES SUGGEST THAT SWITCHBACKS PLAY AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN THE EVOLUTION OF SOLAR WIND. EVIDENCE OF MAGNETIC RECONNECTION AND WAVE ACTIVITIES WAS FOUND AT THE BOUNDARIES OF SWITCHBACKS  AND THESE PROCESSES MAY FACILITATE THE ENERGY DISSIPATION IN THE SWITCHBACKS. SIMULATIONS SHOW THAT THE SWITCHBACKS CAN BE DESTROYED BY PARAMETRIC DECAY  RELEASING ENERGY TO THE BACKGROUND PLASMA. THUS  SWITCHBACKS MAY CONTRIBUTE SIGNIFICANTLY TO THE HEATING AND ACCELERATION OF THE SOLAR WIND. HOWEVER  HOW AND WHERE THE SWITCHBACKS ARE GENERATED IS STILL A MYSTERY  AND A QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS OF THEIR INFLUENCES ON THE BACKGROUND SOLAR WIND IS STILL NEEDED. THE APPEARANCE AND AMPLITUDE OF SWITCHBACKS ARE USUALLY MODULATED BY A LARGE TIME SCALE  TYPICALLY SEVERAL HOURS  SO THAT THE SWITCHBACKS APPEAR IN PATCHES. THESE PATCHES ARE BELIEVED TO BE REMNANTS OF SPATIAL AND/OR TEMPORAL EFFECTS IN THE CORONAL SOURCE REGION OF THE WIND  SO THAT STUDYING THE PATCHES MAY HELP TO UNDERSTAND THE ORIGINS OF SWITCHBACKS. THUS  WE PROPOSE TO ANALYZE IN-SITU SATELLITE MEASUREMENTS OF THE SOLAR WIND AND REMOTE-SENSING OBSERVATIONS OF THE SUN IN ORDER TO ANSWER THE FOLLOWING QUESTIONS: (1) HOW DO THE PROPERTIES OF SWITCHBACKS EVOLVE IN THE SOLAR WIND? WHAT CAN WE LEARN ABOUT THE GENERATION MECHANISMS OF THE SWITCHBACKS FROM THEIR PROPERTIES? (2) HOW MUCH DO THE SWITCHBACKS CONTRIBUTE TO THE ACCELERATION AND HEATING OF THE SOLAR WIND? (3) WHAT IS THE ORIGIN OF THE SWITCHBACK PATCHES? ARE THEY RELATED TO CERTAIN SPATIAL STRUCTURES OR TEMPORAL PROCESSES IN THE SOLAR CORONA? METHODOLOGY: WE WILL COMBINE IN-SITU MEASUREMENTS OF THE SOLAR WIND AND REMOTE SENSING MEASUREMENTS OF THE SOLAR ATMOSPHERE. WE WILL USE INSITU DATA FROM PSP  SOLAR ORBITER AND WIND TO IDENTIFY SWITCHBACKS AND SWITCHBACK PATCHES IN THE SOLAR WIND. THEN WE WILL CONDUCT ANALYSES OF THE PROPERTIES OF SWITCHBACKS AND SWITCHBACK PATCHES  INCLUDING HOW THEY EVOLVE AS THE SOLAR WIND PROPAGATES. WE WILL SELECT TIME INTERVALS WHEN PSP IS GOING THROUGH FAST RADIAL SCAN AND ESTIMATE THE CONTRIBUTION OF THE SWITCHBACKS TO THE ACCELERATION AND HEATING OF THE SOLAR WIND. THE REMOTE SENSING DATA WILL BE FROM HELIOSEISMIC AND MAGNETIC IMAGER (HMI) AND ATMOSPHERIC IMAGING ASSEMBLY (AIA) ONBOARD SOLAR DYNAMICS OBSERVATORY (SDO). WE WILL USE THE REMOTE SENSING DATA  COMBINED WITH TECHNIQUES SUCH AS THE POTENTIAL-FIELD-SOURCE-SURFACE MODEL  TO IDENTIFY SOURCE REGIONS OF THE SOLAR WIND STREAMS MEASURED IN-SITU BY PSP AND OTHER SATELLITES. RELEVANCE: KNOWLEDGE OF THE PROPERTIES AND ORIGINS OF MAGNETIC SWITCHBACKS WILL GREATLY IMPROVE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE ORIGINS OF THE SOLAR WIND AND HOW THE SOLAR WIND IS ACCELERATED AND HEATED. THUS  IT IS DIRECTLY RELATED TO ONE OF THE HELIOPHYSICS OVERARCHING GOALS:  EXPLORE AND CHARACTERIZE THE PHYSICAL PROCESSES IN THE SPACE ENVIRONMENT FROM THE SUN TO THE HELIOPAUSE AND THROUGHOUT THE UNIVERSE.  BESIDES  GENERATION OF THE SWITCHBACKS AND SWITCHBACK PATCHES IS A RESULT OF THE SUN S ACTIVITY  SO THE PROPOSED STUDY WILL ALSO CONTRIBUTE TO THE HELIOPHYSICS OVERARCHING GOAL:  ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE SUN S ACTIVITY.  FURTHERMORE  AS THE SWITCHBACKS MAY PLAY AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN HEATING AND ACCELERATING THE SOLAR WIND AS WELL AS ENERGIZING PARTICLES  THE PROPOSED STUDY WILL HELP US DEVELOP THE KNOWLEDGE AND CAPABILITY TO DETECT AND PREDICT EXTREME CONDITIONS IN SPACE TO PROTECT LIFE AND SOCIETY AND TO SAFEGUARD HUMAN AND ROBOTIC EXPLORERS BEYOND EARTH.

Description: THE NATIONAL ACADEMIES  2018 DECADAL SURVEY FOR EARTH SCIENCE  THRIVING ON OUR CHANGING PLANET  IDENTIFIES IMAGING SPECTROSCOPY AS A NECESSARY MEASUREMENT TO ADDRESS A MOST IMPORTANT OBJECTIVE FOR THE HYDROLOGIC CYCLE: "QUANTIFY RATES OF SNOW ACCUMULATION  SNOWMELT  ICE MELT  AND SUBLIMATION FROM SNOW AND ICE WORLDWIDE AT SCALES DRIVEN BY TOPOGRAPHIC VARIABILITY." MEETING THIS OBJECTIVE REQUIRES THE ABILITY TO MEASURE SNOW ALBEDO AND UNDERSTAND HOW AND WHY IT VARIES  ESPECIALLY IN THE WORLD'S MOUNTAINS  WHICH COMPRISE A QUARTER OF THE WORLD'S LAND AREA BUT PRODUCE AT LEAST HALF OF THE RUNOFF. THE EUROPEAN SPACE AGENCY HAS SELECTED A CANDIDATE SENSOR TO ADDRESS THESE NEEDS. THE COPERNICUS HYPERSPECTRAL IMAGING MISSION FOR THE ENVIRONMENT (CHIME) IS IN PHASE B1  WITH SPATIAL RESOLUTION OF 20 TO 30 M  SPECTRAL COVERAGE FROM 400 TO 2500 NM AT RESOLUTION OF 10 NM OR LESS  REVISIT INTERVAL OF 10 TO 12 DAYS  10:30 EQUATOR CROSSING TIME  LAUNCH 2026. THE PROPOSED INVESTIGATION WILL ADDRESS THE CAPABILITY OF CHIME TO TACKLE THE FOLLOWING QUESTIONS AND HELP DEVELOP APPROPRIATE LEVEL 2 PRODUCTS. EXPERIENCE AND CROSS-VALIDATION WOULD BENEFIT THE DEVELOPMENT OF NASA S SURFACE BIOLOGY AND GEOLOGY DESIGNATED OBSERVABLE AND SHORTEN THE REVISIT INTERVAL. Q1. HOW DOES SENSITIVITY OF IMAGING SPECTROSCOPY RETRIEVALS OF SNOW AND GLACIER PROPERTIES IN THE MOUNTAINS VARY DEPENDING ON THE SOLUTION METHOD FOR THE INVERSION AND THE ATMOSPHERIC CORRECTION? Q2. HOW DO SNOW SPECIFIC SURFACE AREA  RADIATIVE FORCING BY LIGHT-ABSORBING PARTICLES  AND SNOW ALBEDO VARY SPATIALLY  SEASONALLY  AND INTERANNUALLY IN THE WORLD'S MOUNTAINS? Q3. HOW CAN A FUSION OF SPECTROSCOPY DATA WITH MORE FREQUENT AND BROADER COVERAGE FROM MULTISPECTRAL SENSORS ENABLE CHARACTERIZATION OF THE SNOW AND ICE PROPERTIES AND RADIATIVE FORCING OVER LARGER AREAS AND ACROSS SEASONS AND YEARS? THE CORRESPONDING OBJECTIVES ARE: O1. USE CHIME S SURFACE REFLECTANCE PRODUCTS  CORRECTED FOR TOPOGRAPHY  TO INVERT THE SIGNAL FOR RETRIEVAL OF SNOW PROPERTIES  AND THEREBY INFORM ESA OF FEASIBLE LEVEL 2 PRODUCTS FOR SNOW AND GLACIER PROPERTIES. O2. PRE-LAUNCH ANALYZE SPATIAL VARIABILITY OF SNOW SPECIFIC SURFACE AREA  RADIATIVE FORCING BY DUST  CARBON  AND ORGANIC MATERIAL  AND RESULTING SNOW AND ICE ALBEDO USING AVAILABLE DATA FROM AIRBORNE SPECTROMETERS. POST-LAUNCH PLAN SIMILAR ANALYSES GLOBALLY IN REPRESENTATIVE MOUNTAIN RANGES. O3. Description: GEOSTATIONARY CARBON CYCLE OBSERVATORY (GEOCARB) MISSION. NASA HAS SELECTED A FIRST-OF-ITS-KIND EARTH SCIENCE MISSION THAT WILL EXTEND OUR NATION'S LEAD IN MEASURING KEY GREENHOUSE GASES AND VEGETATION HEALTH FROM SPACE TO ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF EARTH'S NATURAL EXCHANGES OF CARBON BETWEEN THE LAND, ATMOSPHERE AND OCEAN. THE PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR (PI)-LED MISSION WILL LAUNCH ON A COMMERCIAL COMMUNICATIONS SATELLITE TO MAKE OBSERVATIONS OVER THE AMERICAS FROM AN ORBIT OF APPROXIMATELY 22,000 MILES (35,400 KILOMETERS) ABOVE THE EQUATOR. THE MISSION WAS COMPETITIVELY SELECTED FROM 15 PROPOSALS SUBMITTED TO THE AGENCY'S SECOND EARTH VENTURE - MISSION ANNOUNCEMENT OF OPPORTUNITY FOR SMALL ORBITAL INVESTIGATIONS OF THE EARTH SYSTEM.  THE PRIMARY GOALS OF THE GEOCARB MISSION ARE TO MONITOR PLANT HEALTH AND VEGETATION STRESS THROUGHOUT THE AMERICAS, TO PROBE, IN UNPRECEDENTED DETAIL, THE NATURAL SOURCES, SINKS AND EXCHANGE PROCESSES THAT CONTROL CARBON DIOXIDE, CARBON MONOXIDE AND METHANE IN THE ATMOSPHERE, AND TO PROVIDE OBSERVATIONS AND DEMONSTRATE METHODS TO REALIZE A TRANSFORMATIONAL ADVANCE IN THE SCIENTIFIC UNDERSTANDING OF THE GLOBAL CARBON CYCLE.  THE GEOCARB MISSION, A CATEGORY 3 MISSION (PER NPR 7120.5E, NASA SPACE FLIGHT PROGRAM AND PROJECT MANAGEMENT REQUIREMENTS) WITH A CLASS D PAYLOAD (PER NPR 8705.4, RISK CLASSIFICATION FOR NASA PAYLOADS), IS A SCIENCE INVESTIGATION WITH THE PRIMARY OBJECTIVE OF SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVING KNOWLEDGE OF TERRESTRIAL FLUXES OF CO2 AND CH4 AT SCIENCE- AND POLICY-RELEVANT SCALES. THE GEOCARB MISSION UTILIZES A MULTI-CHANNEL SLIT-SCAN SPECTROMETER BASED INSTRUMENT THAT WILL MEASURE ABSORPTION SPECTRA IN SUNLIGHT REFLECTED FROM THE GROUND TO INFER THE ATMOSPHERE-COLUMN CONCENTRATIONS OF CO2, CH4, AND CARBON MONOXIDE (CO). THE INSTRUMENT WILL ALSO MEASURE SOLAR-INDUCED FLUORESCENCE (SIF), WHICH PROVIDES DIRECT INFORMATION ABOUT PHOTOSYNTHESIS.  THE CONTRACTOR AND ITS TEAM MEMBERS WILL PERFORM THE FULL NASA LIFE CYCLE FORMULATION AND IMPLEMENTATION PHASES A THROUGH F. THE GEOCARB PROPOSAL WAS SELECTED UNDER THE NASA ANNOUNCEMENT OF OPPORTUNITY NNH15ZDA011O FOR THE EARTH VENTURE MISSION - 2 ELEMENT OF THE EARTH SYSTEM SCIENCE PATHFINDER PROGRAM OFFICES EARTH VENTURE LINE.

Description: CLAY MINERALS PRESENT A CONUNDRUM ON MARS- WHILE WE OBSERVE RELATIVELY THICK LAYERS OF CLAY MINERALS AND OTHER SECONDARY MINERALS WHICH ARE TYPICALLY FORMED THROUGH AQUEOUS PROCESSES ON EARTH  CLIMATE MODELS PREDICT COLD CONDITIONS ON EARLY MARS THAT PRECLUDE LONG-TERM STABILITY OF FRESH WATER ON THE SURFACE. ADDING SALT DECREASES THE FREEZING POINT OF WATER  ALLOWING LONG-TERM STABILITY OF LIQUID WATER AT COLDER TEMPERATURES AND LOWER PRESSURES. SALTS ALSO ALLOW FOR THIN FILMS OF WATER AT MINERAL SURFACES. PREVIOUS EXPERIMENTS CONDUCTED BY OUR RESEARCH GROUP DEMONSTRATE THAT MINERAL-BRINE INTERACTIONS CAN PRODUCE CLAY MINERALS WITHIN WEEKS OF REACTION WITH PRIMARY ROCK-FORMING SILICATES. HERE WE AIM TO FURTHER INVESTIGATE THE MINERALOGY AND ABUNDANCE OF CLAY MINERAL PHASES PRODUCED WHEN PRIMARY SILICATE MINERALS REACT WITH HIGH SALINITY BRINES. IN ADDITION  WE WILL ALSO EXAMINE CLAY ALTERATION IN HIGH SALINITY BRINES TO FURTHER UNDERSTAND THE POTENTIAL EFFECTS OF EVAPORATING/FREEZING SURFACE WATERS AS WELL AS HIGH DENSITY DIAGENETIC FLUIDS ON CLAY MINERALOGY AND CHEMISTRY. OUR PREVIOUS MINERAL-BRINE DISSOLUTION EXPERIMENTS WERE DESIGNED TO MEASURE PRIMARY MINERAL WEATHERING RATES IN HIGH SALINITY FLUIDS. WHILE SECONDARY CLAY MINERALS WERE OBSERVED AT THE MICRON SCALE VIA SCANNING ELECTRON MICROSCOPY (SEM) AND RAMAN SPECTROSCOPY  THEY PROVED DIFFICULT TO FULLY ANALYZE USING X-RAY DIFFRACTION (XRD) METHODS DUE TO THEIR LIMITED ABUNDANCE. HERE  WE PROPOSE TO CONDUCT LONGER-TERM BRINE WEATHERING EXPERIMENTS USING SIGNIFICANTLY LARGER QUANTITIES OF REACTANTS  INCLUDING PYROXENE  OLIVINE  PLAGIOCLASE FELDSPAR  MAFIC SILICATE GLASS  AND BASALT IN ORDER TO PRODUCE SUFFICIENT REACTION PRODUCTS NEEDED TO CHARACTERIZE THE SECONDARY MINERALS USING A WIDE RANGE OF ANALYTICAL TECHNIQUES. FURTHERMORE  WE WILL EXPLORE THE ROLE OF BRINE CHEMISTRY ON CLAY DIAGENESIS AND WEATHERING BY REACTING CLAY MINERALS WITH THE BRINES. MINERAL AND ROCK SAMPLES WILL BE REACTED WITH NEAR-SATURATED BRINES AND 1:10 DILUTED SOLUTIONS OF NACL  NA2SO4  NACLO4  CACL2  MGCL2  MGSO4  AND NH4CL OVER 6 MONTHS  THEN FILTERED TO COLLECT THE SOLID AND LIQUID REACTION PRODUCTS. ADDITIONAL HIGH TEMPERATURE (350K FOR 50 DAYS) AND LOW TEMPERATURE EXPERIMENTS (250K FOR 450 DAYS) WILL BE CONDUCTED WITH BASALT AND MAFIC GLASS. THE CLAY-SIZED FRACTION WILL BE SEPARATED VIA WET SIEVING AND CENTRIFUGE TECHNIQUES. SIMILAR EXPERIMENTS WILL ALSO BE CONDUCTED USING CLAY STANDARDS (KAOLINITE  NONTRONITE  SMECTITE  CHLORITE). THE MINERALOGY OF THE REACTION PRODUCTS WILL BE DETERMINED USING X-RAY DIFFRACTION OF BOTH RANDOM POWDERS AND ORIENTED CLAY MOUNTS (WITH AND WITHOUT HEAT AND GLYCOL TREATMENTS)  AS WELL AS RAMAN SPECTROSCOPY. BULK CHEMISTRY OF THE CLAY-SIZED FRACTION WILL BE DETERMINED VIA ICP OPTICAL EMISSION SPECTROSCOPY ANALYSIS OF DIGESTIONS. WE WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE REACTION PRODUCT MINERALOGY  MORPHOLOGY  CHEMISTRY AND TEXTURAL RELATIONSHIPS USING BOTH SCANNING AND TRANSMISSION ELECTRON MICROSCOPY. THESE EXPERIMENTS WILL INFORM OUR UNDERSTANDING OF POTENTIAL MINERAL-BRINE INTERACTIONS ON MARS AND OTHER SALTY WORLDS  INCLUDING CERES  EUROPA  AND ENCELADUS AND WILL PROVIDE RICHER CONTEXT FOR INTERPRETING MINERAL ASSEMBLAGES AND SEDIMENTARY ROCKS  INCLUDING CLAY MINERALS  OBSERVED ON THESE BODIES. THUS  THIS WORK IS RELEVANT TO THE SSW PROGRAM AS IT INVESTIGATES  GEOCHEMICAL PROCESSES OCCURRING ON PLANETARY BODIES  SATELLITES  AND OTHER MINOR BODIES  AND SEEKS TO  INFORM OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE FUNDAMENTAL PROCESSES AT WORK BY CHARACTERIZING AND UNDERSTANDING  THE CHEMICAL  MINERALOGICAL  AND PHYSICAL FEATURES OF PLANETARY SURFACES (SUCH AS GEOLOGIC FORMATIONS AND IMPACT CRATERS) AND FLUID INVENTORIES THAT INTERACT WITH THE SURFACE (INCLUDING HYDROSPHERES  CRYOSPHERES  ATMOSPHERES  AND OTHER VOLATILE RESERVOIRS).  AND DEVELOPS  THEORETICAL AND EXPERIMENTAL BASES FOR UNDERSTANDING THESE FEATURES IN THE CONTEXT OF THE VARYING CONDITIONS THROUGH TIME AFTER FORMATION.
